title: A Warrior’s View of Why War Fails
author: William H. McRaven
text: Podcast A Warrior’s View of Why War FailsA Conversation with William McRaven Published on October 29, 2026 Play Listen to the Episode 59 minutes 00:00 / 59:09 0.5×1×1.5×2× MP3 Close audio player Print Print this article Save Sign in and save to read later Close Share A Warrior’s View of Why War Fails A Conversation with William McRaven Share in email Share on Facebook Share on X Share on LinkedIn Article link: https://www.foreignaffairs.com/podcasts/warriors-view-why-war-fails-william-mcravenhttps://www.foreignaffairs.com/podcasts/warriors-view-why-war-fails-william-mcraven Request reprint permissions here.Episode Details William McRaven spent four decades in the U.S. military as a Navy SEAL, a four-star admiral, and head of U.S. Special Operations Command. He led the 2003 operation that captured Saddam Hussein and oversaw the 2011 operation that killed Osama bin Laden. But in a new essay in Foreign Affairs, McRaven focuses not on the potential of military force but on its limits—limits that American policymakers frequently disregard, at immense cost. He warns of a persistent “American delusion—our excessive faith in the capacity of military power to achieve victory and thereby fundamentally political ends.” And while the Trump administration’s war in Iran may offer a particularly stark example of this delusion, McRaven worries that the problem will get worse rather than better in the future.Dan Kurtz-Phelan spoke with McRaven on October 26 about the wars in Iran and Ukraine; about the damage to civil-military relations and military culture under President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth; about how technology is, and is not, transforming the battlefield; and about the risks of a strictly transactional foreign policy for the durability of American power.Sources:“The Limits of American Power” by William H. McRaven“Made in the Alliance” by William H.
